feedback: When the child labels 85p as 'change', separate the quantities on the bar — the £1 whole, the 85p cost part, the change part — and label each, then ask which quantity the question wants
If the child stops at 85p, prompt: 'you found the cost — what does the question still want?'
If the child accepts 85p as change without checking, ask: 'could your change be 85p if you spent 85p from a pound?' to build the sense-check habit
Confirm when the child names 85p as cost, computes 15p change, attaches the unit, and checks that 85p + 15p makes the £1 paid
activities.intendedInsight: In a multi-step problem each number along the way means something specific; the answer is only right when you name the quantity the question actually asked for and check it is reasonable in context.
learnerActions: Set up a shopping problem: two items at 65p and 20p, paying with £1
Choose a representation and say why it fits (e.g. a bar model with a £1 whole, an 85p part for the shopping, and a mystery part)
Pause at the interim number and label it: 'that 85p — what is it?' Answer: the total cost (65p + 20p = 85p)
Carry on to the second step: change £1 into 100p, then work out 100p − 85p = 15p as the change
Interpret the final number with its unit ('15p change') and sense-check it: the cost and the change together should make the £1 paid (85p + 15p = 100p = £1)
Transfer: re-run the model paying with £2 instead and describe what changes
activities.title: Multi-step money modeller: name the quantity, then check it

feedback: If the child accepts the shopkeeper's framing, ask them to point to where the cost ends and the change begins
Prompt the child to restate the final quantity with its unit and say how they know it is reasonable
This dialogue is never scored — treat it as thinking-out-loud practice
activities.intendedInsight: Distinguishing which quantity the answer names is a reasoning skill you can articulate and defend, not just compute.
learnerActions: Play out a shop exchange where a shopkeeper rings up two items and states the subtotal as if it were the change
Catch and correct the error out loud, explaining which quantity the stated number actually is
Keep units straight (pounds and pence) while justifying the fix
Explain aloud how a bar or equation would separate the cost from the change
activities.title: Shopkeeper who tries it on (spoken correction)

feedback: If the child reads a value but doesn't tie it to the question, ask 'what does this number tell you about the objects you measured?'
Prompt a units and reasonableness check on the answer read from the plot
activities.intendedInsight: A data display is a representation you read answers from; the answer must be interpreted back into the real-world question with its units.
learnerActions: Collect or receive measurement data (e.g. lengths of objects)
Create a line plot displaying the data
Use the plot to answer a real-world question, reading the answer off the display back into the situation
State what quantity your answer represents and whether it is reasonable
activities.title: Line plot from measurement data
